name: SUMO (Simulation of Urban MObility)
maintainer: German Aerospace Center (DLR) Institute of Transportation Systems, hosted as an Eclipse Foundation project (eclipse-sumo on GitHub), plus community contributors
first_release: 2001 (SUMO docs state the package has been used since 2001; copyright line 2001-2026)
last_activity: v1.28.0 released 2026-10-08 (ChangeLog); GitHub main branch pushed 2026-11-11
licence: EPL-2.0 (GitHub licence detection and SUMO at a Glance). A secondary GPL-2.0-or-later option is often cited [uncertain]
language: C++ core (sumo, netconvert, sumo-gui); Python tooling (osmWebWizard, randomTrips, traci client). GitHub reports Python as the top language by bytes
code_availability: Source with public repository: https://github.com/eclipse-sumo/sumo; binaries for Windows/macOS/Linux; pip packages (eclipse-sumo, libsumo, traci)
maintenance_health: Very healthy. Releases roughly every 1-4 months (1.27.0 on 2026-05-21, 1.27.1 on 2026-06-25, 1.28.0 on 2026-10-08), daily commits, about 4.3k GitHub stars, active sumo-user mailing list with maintainer replies. The ChangeLog still lists sublane deadlock fixes in 1.28.0 and Git main, so the sublane model is still being hardened
scale: Microscopic by default; a mesoscopic mode (queue-based, up to 100 times faster per the docs) is available
car_following: Default Krauss (safe-speed model, parameters accel, decel, emergencyDecel, sigma for driver imperfection, tau for reaction headway, minGap). Alternatives include IDM, EIDM, ACC, CACC, Wiedemann (W99) and others selectable per vType through carFollowModel
lane_model: Lane-based by default: vehicles sit at the lane centre and change lanes instantly (LC2013 model). Option --lanechange.duration gives continuous, non-instant lane changes. Option --lateral-resolution switches on the sublane model with the SL2015 lane-change model
lateral_model_type: Sublane. With --lateral-resolution <m> (default -1 = off) each lane is split into sublanes, and vehicles may hold any lateral offset. SL2015 parameters: lcSublane (default 1.0), lcPushy (0-1, default 0), lcAssertive (0-1, default 0), lcImpatience, lcTimeToImpatience, lcAccelLat, lcMaxSpeedLatStanding, lcMaxSpeedLatFactor. vType attributes minGapLat, latAlignment (right, center, left, arbitrary, compact, nice, or offset) and maxSpeedLat. The resolution should divide lane width evenly (0.8 m gives 4 sublanes on a 3.2 m lane) and be small enough for the narrowest vehicle
junction_model: Junctions have internal lanes. Right-of-way comes from the node type (priority, right_before_left, allway_stop, zipper, traffic_light, and others) and edge priority. Minor-road vehicles wait at the lane end and accept gaps using jmTimegapMinor (default 1 s). Other junction-model vType parameters: jmCrossingGap (10 m), jmIgnoreKeepClearTime (-1), jmDriveAfterYellowTime and jmDriveAfterRedTime (-1), jmIgnoreFoeProb and jmIgnoreFoeSpeed (0), jmIgnoreJunctionFoeProb (0), jmSigmaMinor, jmStoplineGap (1 m), and impatience (0, grows over --time-to-impatience, default 180 s). A keep-clear (no-block) heuristic is on by default (--default.junctions.keep-clear true) and can be turned off per node or connection. Roundabouts give circulating edges priority, detected by --roundabouts.guess (default true, max circumference 3500 m)
signal_control_modes: Static fixed-time programs, actuated (gap-based), delay_based, NEMA dual-ring and others. netconvert can guess signals from OSM (--tls.guess-signals, --tls.default-type actuated). Programs can be changed at runtime through TraCI/libsumo, which is the standard hook for RL controllers (for example sumo-rl and Flow)
flyover_support: Yes. Edges that cross without sharing a node do not interact, so flyovers, bridges and underpasses work. netconvert --ramps.guess adds acceleration and deceleration lanes on motorway on- and off-ramps. Merges and diverges are ordinary junctions; zipper nodes are available for merges
grade_separation_handling: OSM import: --osm.layer-elevation reads the OSM layer tag into z-coordinates through a heuristic, and the docs warn that manual correction may be needed. SRTM and other elevation sources can be imported. Dual carriageways split by a median produce clusters of junctions that should be merged with --junctions.join, or the short internal edges cause throughput loss, jams and deadlocks. Fixes are applied with netedit or plain-XML patch files (nodes, edges, connections, roundabout definitions). Exact z-handling for crossing ways without a layer tag [uncertain]
vehicle_types: Built-in vClasses include passenger, bus, coach, truck, trailer, delivery, taxi, motorcycle, moped, bicycle, pedestrian, emergency, tram and rail. Each vType sets length, width, minGap, accel, decel, maxSpeed, speedFactor, speedDev, carFollowModel, laneChangeModel, emissionClass and lateral attributes. Custom types (for example auto-rickshaw or e-rickshaw) are defined by cloning a vClass and changing dimensions and dynamics. Lane permissions use allow/disallow per vClass
gridlock_policy: Teleporting: a vehicle that is first in line and slower than 0.1 m/s for --time-to-teleport (default 300 s; values of 0 or below disable it) leaves the network and reappears downstream. Extras: --time-to-teleport.highways (default 0 = off), .disconnected, .bidi, .remove (delete instead of teleport), --max-num-teleports (abort above the limit, default -1). --ignore-junction-blocker <s> (default -1) ignores vehicles stuck inside a junction. --collision.action defaults to teleport. Teleports are reported as warnings with a reason (wrong lane, yield, jam, blocked, disconnected), counted in summary output and meanData, and absent from FCD output
mixed_traffic_support: Partial. Vehicles of different widths can share a lane side by side under the sublane model, and per-type minGapLat and latAlignment shape lateral spacing. This is the closest any mainstream open-source simulator gets to Indian mixed traffic, but it is still anchored to lane geometry and was designed for bicycles and motorcycles in otherwise lane-disciplined traffic
non_lane_behaviour: Approximated through the sublane model: vehicles drift continuously across sublanes, overtake within a lane, and set a preferred lateral alignment. Lane markings stay as the network topology (one wide lane per carriageway is a common workaround to mimic no-lane roads). Behaviour at junctions is still governed by connections from specific lanes, so free-form weaving through an intersection is not modelled. A truly continuous 2D model does not exist in SUMO
seepage_filtering_support: Possible through the sublane model. Narrow vehicles with small minGapLat, latAlignment arbitrary or compact, and lcPushy/lcAssertive above 0 can filter between queued cars toward the stop line. Calibration of this behaviour for Indian motorcycles in SUMO is not documented in official sources [uncertain]
per_class_parameters: SUMO publishes generic vClass defaults (Vehicle Type Parameter Defaults page). For example the speedDev default is 0.1 for most classes and 0.05 for trucks. No official Indian per-class set (two-wheeler, three-wheeler, bus, LCV) is shipped; these must come from Indian studies such as Indo-HCM or calibrated papers [uncertain]
indian_calibration_evidence: A calibration of SUMO for Indian heterogeneous traffic on a 2 km segment in Chennai reportedly gave results comparable with a calibrated VISSIM on the same test bed (IIT Madras listing; full text not verified) [uncertain]. SiMTraM (IIT Bombay, 2013-2015) extended SUMO with strips and validated it on Mumbai data. Similar SUMO class-specific calibrations exist for Dhaka (motorcycles, rickshaws, CNG three-wheelers) and Sri Lanka (MAPE/GEH on 15-minute counts). None of these found used the SL2015 sublane model specifically [uncertain]
calibration_dataset_used: Chennai 2 km urban segment (data not confirmed open) [uncertain]; Mumbai Eastern Express Highway video data for SiMTraM (not open) [uncertain]
calibration_method: SUMO ships calibration helpers (routeSampler, flowrouter, calibrator objects for live count matching). Indian studies report manual or sensitivity-based parameter tuning against travel time and flow; GEH and MAPE are common metrics in South Asian SUMO studies [uncertain]
max_density_tested: No published Indian density limit for SUMO sublane found [uncertain]
validation_against_field_case: Chennai 2 km segment compared with VISSIM [uncertain]; no SUMO validation against Hebbal or Silk Board found [uncertain]
network_import: netconvert imports OpenStreetMap, OpenDRIVE, VISUM, Vissim, MATsim, shapefiles and plain XML. Recommended OSM options: --geometry.remove --ramps.guess --junctions.join --tls.guess-signals --tls.discard-simple --tls.join --tls.default-type actuated, plus --lefthand for India and typemaps for road classes. osmWebWizard.py gives a browser map picker that downloads OSM, runs netconvert, generates randomTrips demand per mode (passenger, bus, truck, motorcycle, bicycle, pedestrian and others), writes osm.net.xml and osm.sumocfg, and launches sumo-gui. Very large areas make it slow
demand_input_formats: XML routes (vehicle, trip, flow, route, vType, routeDistribution), trips with origin/destination edges routed by duarouter, flows with vehsPerHour/period/probability, OD matrices through od2trips, detector counts through routeSampler or flowrouter, activity-based demand through activitygen, randomTrips.py for synthetic demand, and runtime insertion through TraCI
runs_in_browser_or_server: Server or desktop native process. No browser build; web front-ends talk to a server-side SUMO through TraCI/libsumo (for example the archived sidewalklabs/sumo-web3d, which used TraCI plus three.js)
wasm_or_streaming_feasibility: No official or maintained WebAssembly build was found [uncertain]. The practical pattern is to run SUMO or libsumo on a server and stream vehicle positions (FCD-like subscriptions) to the browser over WebSocket, or run the batch and replay FCD output client-side. Compiling the C++ core with Emscripten is theoretically possible but untested and risky inside 72 hours
api: TraCI: a TCP socket protocol with clients in Python, C++ (libtraci), Java, Matlab and others. It supports multiple clients and remote control of vehicles, signals, routes and edges, and subscriptions. libsumo: an in-process C++ library with Python (pip install libsumo), Java and C++ bindings and the same function signatures, but no socket overhead. libsumo cannot serve multiple clients, has experimental or no GUI support, and needs Python multiprocessing for parallel instances
performance: The docs claim up to 100,000 vehicle updates per second on a 1 GHz CPU (old figure). Mesoscopic mode is up to 100 times faster. --threads exists for parallel simulation. Smaller --lateral-resolution values increase computation time. City-scale scenarios with tens of thousands of vehicles commonly run faster than real time without the GUI [uncertain]
multi_tenancy_model: One SUMO process per scenario run (TraCI server or libsumo inside a worker process). Hosting cost scales with concurrent runs; batch runs with a step cap are cheap. Interactive sessions hold one process per user. Use a worker pool or queue with time and step limits
build_complexity: Low if using prebuilt packages: pip install eclipse-sumo libsumo traci, apt packages, or the official Docker images. Building from source needs CMake, Xerces-C, PROJ, GDAL, FOX (GUI) and Eigen, which takes moderate effort. Embedding through libsumo in Python is straightforward
scenario_editability: Through netedit or plain XML or the TraCI API: lanes (count, width, permissions per vClass), speeds, edge priority, junction type and keepClear, connections, traffic-light programs and phases, demand (routes, flows, vTypes), bus stops, parking areas, detectors, rerouters, calibrators, variable speed signs. netconvert can regenerate the net from edited plain-XML node/edge/connection files
output_metrics_supported: Trip info (travel time, waiting time, time loss/delay, departDelay), summary (running, waiting, teleports, mean speed), edge and lane meanData (density, occupancy, speed, flow, timeLoss, waitingTime, teleports), queue output (queue length per lane), induction-loop and lane-area detectors, FCD trajectories, emissions output, SSM device for conflicts (TTC, DRAC, PET), and TLS state. Dynamic PCU and Indian LOS are not built in and must be derived
emissions_support: Yes: HBEFA v2.1, v3.1 and v4.2 based classes, plus PHEMlight and PHEMlight5, with an emissions device and outputs
reuse_mode: Use as engine. SUMO runs server-side as the simulation core; we build the web UI, scenario editor and metrics layer around netconvert, sumo/libsumo and its XML outputs
effort_within_72_hours: Realistic and recommended. About 4-6 hours for a Docker image with SUMO plus a Python (FastAPI) worker using libsumo/TraCI, about 6-10 hours for the OSM-to-net pipeline (netconvert with the recommended options and --lefthand, bounded bbox), and about 10-16 hours for a web map UI that streams vehicle positions and edits lanes, widths, signals and demand by regenerating plain XML. Indian vTypes (2W, 3W, car, bus, truck) with sublane at 0.8-1.0 m resolution take about 2-4 hours. Cut: in-browser simulation, a full netedit-equivalent editor, rigorous calibration, mesoscopic mode, and emission dashboards beyond the default HBEFA output
licence_constraint: EPL-2.0 is weak file-level copyleft. Modifications to SUMO source files must be published under EPL when distributed, but our own separate web app and orchestration code can use any licence. Running SUMO unmodified on a server (SaaS) triggers no source obligation. Keep any SUMO patches upstream or in a public fork
known_limitations: The sublane model is still lane-anchored, not true 2D, and costs more CPU at fine resolution. Sublane deadlocks and unsafe driving were still being fixed in 1.28.0 and Git main. OSM networks need cleanup: junction clusters on divided roads, missing turn lanes, wrong lane counts, layer heuristics for flyovers. libsumo has no multi-client or stable GUI support. No WebAssembly build. No built-in Indian vehicle classes or dynamic PCU
documented_failures: OSM imports without --junctions.join produce short intermediate edges that cause throughput loss, jams and deadlocks (OSM import docs). A bicycle path crossing a roundabout stopped netconvert from detecting it, so entering vehicles got priority and the roundabout deadlocked (sumo-user list). Many connections with keepClear=false caused deadlocks (sumo-user list). Vehicles inserted on the wrong lane near turn bays get stuck; the docs recommend departLane=best. The ChangeLog records fixed deadlocks with parallel internal lanes (1.27.1) and in sublane simulation (1.28.0)
validation_approach: Extensive nightly regression test suite (TextTest) with published daily test and coverage reports, plus a body of peer-reviewed calibration studies by users, including Indian ones
takeaway_for_our_build: Adopt SUMO as the engine, run it server-side through libsumo or TraCI in one worker process per scenario, and stream positions to the browser. Always run OSM through netconvert with --junctions.join --ramps.guess --tls.guess-signals --tls.join --lefthand and a bounded bbox. Enable the sublane model (--lateral-resolution about 0.8 m) with explicit Indian vTypes. Never hide teleports: surface teleport counts and reasons as a first-class 'model health' metric next to delay and queue results
